App::HTTPThis: the tiny web server I keep reaching for
entry.summary:
Whenever I’m building a static website, I almost never start by reaching for Apache, nginx, Docker, or anything that feels like “proper infrastructure”. Nine times out of ten I just want a directory served over HTTP so I can click around, test routes, check assets, and see what happens in a real browser. For that job, I’ve been using App::HTTPThis for years. It’s a simple local web server you run from the command line. Point it at a directory, and it serves it. That’s it. No vhosts. No config bureaucracy. No “why is this module not enabled”. Just: run a command and you’ve got a website. Static sites are deceptively simple… right up until they aren’t. entry.title: Cuando las decisiones de la IA se alejan de la responsabilidad humana, la gobernanza falla
entry.summary: Uno de los riesgos más críticos en los sistemas habilitados por inteligencia artificial no es el fallo técnico. Una gobernanza efectiva de la IA exige que toda decisión relevante permanezca trazable a una responsabilidad humana, incluso cuando está respaldada por analítica avanzada, automatización o sistemas de aprendizaje. entry.title: When AI Decisions Drift Away From Human Accountability, Governance Fails
entry.summary: One of the most critical risks in AI-enabled systems is not technical failure. As systems become more complex, responsibility often becomes diffuse. In security-critical and governance-sensitive environments, this separation is dangerous. Effective AI governance requires that every meaningful decision remains traceable to human responsibility — even when supported by advanced analytics, automation, or learning systems. Without this linkage, governance loses its anchor. With it, governance retains legitimacy, control, and trust.
